messages.author: 23313ddbbd484950
messages.subject: truncated contours in density2d
parts:
Dear all,

I 'm creating a 2d density plot using geom_density2d. The contours get
truncated at min and max values of the data. Is there any way around
this, i.e. allow the contours to close?

Thanks in advance,

Christina

messages.author: 23313ddbbd484950
messages.subject: Re: truncated contours in density2d
parts:
Sorry for not providing code before. For example:

V1<-rnorm(20, mean=0.6, sd=0.01)
V2<-rnorm(20, mean=0.2, sd=0.01)
data=data.frame(V1,V2)
plot<-ggplot(data, aes(V1,V2))+ geom_density2d()+ opts(aspect.ratio =
1)+scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0.1,0.3))
+scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0.5,0.7))

Here, I deliberately set the axes limits in order to show what I 'm
looking for. I 'd like to be able to get the contours to close.

Thanks again,
Christina

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: truncated contours in density2d
parts:
No, because the underlying R function, contourLines, doesn't supply
that information. It wouldn't be too hard to figure out how to do it
yourself - you need to look at the contours and figure out whether or
not they need closing, and if so, which sides they need to enclose.
If you do figure it out, I'd be very happy to include the code in
ggplot2.

Hadley
